title: A Phone Call About Moving to the Countryside
script: Sari: [warmly] Wira, my brother, are you serious about leaving the city? You've built your whole career there over the last six years.
Wira: I know it sounds sudden, but I've actually been thinking about it since last spring, not just this week.
Sari: [concerned] What changed your mind? You always said city life suited you perfectly.
Wira: It did, until it didn't anymore. I started feeling exhausted in a way that sleep couldn't fix, and I couldn't explain why.
Sari: [honestly] Was there a specific moment when you realized something needed to change?
Wira: Yes, actually. A farm visit felt restorative, but my doctor also said continuing exhaustion deserved assessment instead of a quick lifestyle diagnosis.
Sari: [relieved] That's a strong sign, I suppose. What exactly do you plan to do out there for work?
Wira: My family and I are considering a three-month rental trial. We will test remote work, school travel, health-care access, costs, and daily routines before deciding.
Sari: [thoughtful] You, waking up early to feed chickens? I honestly can't picture it, although I'd love to see it happen.
Wira: Neither can I completely, but that's exactly why I want to try it, before I become too settled to change anything.
Sari: [reflective] Won't you miss the convenience, though? Restaurants, transportation, everything so close to your apartment?
Wira: Probably, at first. But I think I'll gain something more valuable, like actual silence and real stars at night.
Sari: [peacefully] I remember when we were children, before the city lights, we could see so many stars from Grandmother's roof.
Wira: Exactly that memory is part of why I'm doing this. If the plan suits the whole family, I would like my daughter to know darker skies, not just streetlights.
Sari: [encouraging] When you explain it that way, it makes much more sense to me now.
Wira: Thank you for listening while I test the idea carefully instead of treating one weekend as proof, like everyone else has this month.
Sari: You've always known your own mind, Wira. Just promise you'll visit, and send me photos of those chickens.

quiz.question: How long had Wira been thinking about moving before this call?
quiz.explanation: Wira says he had been thinking about it since last spring, not just this week.

quiz.question: What made Wira start feeling exhausted in the city?
options: A tiredness that sleep couldn't fix, which he couldn't explain
quiz.explanation: He says he started feeling exhausted in a way that sleep couldn't fix, without a clear reason.

quiz.question: What happened when Wira visited his friend's farm?
options: He slept better in one weekend than he had in months at home
He decided farming was too hard
quiz.explanation: He slept better during that one weekend on the farm than he had in months at home in the city.

quiz.question: What does Wira plan to do for work in the countryside?
options: Manage things remotely and eventually grow vegetables and keep chickens
Commute back to the city daily
quiz.explanation: He plans to manage things remotely for now, and eventually grow vegetables and keep a few chickens.

quiz.question: Why does Wira want his daughter to grow up in the countryside?
options: So she can see stars, not just streetlights
So she can attend a better school
So she can learn farming as a job
quiz.explanation: Wira says he wants his daughter to grow up seeing stars, not just streetlights, like he remembers from his grandmother's roof.

quiz.question: Why is one good farm weekend insufficient evidence?
options: Short visits differ from daily life and do not explain continuing exhaustion
quiz.explanation: A pleasant break cannot answer every health or lifestyle question.

quiz.question: What should Wira do about exhaustion first?
options: Leave work before speaking to family
Seek appropriate health assessment rather than assume the city is the cause
quiz.explanation: Persistent unexplained fatigue deserves proper evaluation.

quiz.question: What will the trial period test?
options: Work access, schooling, transport, health care, and family routines
Whether vegetables grow in one week
quiz.explanation: The plan examines ordinary needs, not only scenery.

quiz.question: Whose agreement matters before a move?
options: Wira’s whole household, including his daughter’s needs
quiz.explanation: A family relocation should not be a single person’s escape plan.

quiz.question: What remains attractive after practical checks?
options: Quiet, outdoor space, and a different daily rhythm
quiz.explanation: The revised script keeps genuine values without promising a cure.
